correctness.rationale: The object is defined explicitly over F_19. Exact replay verifies outdegree 9 and four common out-neighbors for every pair, so it satisfies the doubly regular hypothesis of Govc's order-19 classification. All 2,242 nonempty transitive faces are exhaustively enumerated with face vector (19,171,684,1026,342) and Euler characteristic -152, selecting the published homotopy type \(\bigvee^{154}S^3\vee S^4\) rather than \(\bigvee^{135}S^3\). Boundary ranks are independently reproduced over five prime fields. Every one of the 171 affine maps is checked edge-by-edge, and signed fixed-face traces give Lefschetz values -152, 0, and 1 in the three stated classes. The one-dimensional \(H_4\) character is trivial because the acting group has odd order, so Lefschetz gives the asserted \(H_3\) character. The C_19 rational decomposition follows uniquely from the two rational irreducible characters.

value.rationale: The order-19 line is the first published doubly regular case with two distinct nonequivariant homotopy types, so identifying the canonical Paley tournament is a natural structural question rather than an arbitrary finite slice. The affine symmetry is intrinsic to Paley tournaments, and its exact homology character distinguishes information that the wedge type forgets. The result therefore turns an anonymous classification row into a named canonical example and supplies a reusable equivariant invariant across all 171 natural affine symmetries, with an exact C_19-module decomposition.
